turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son's zero went into the gradebook before anyone called me.
I'm not upset, Hale. I asked who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in. I'm writing down that you haven't answered.
But I'm not changing the grade.
Then tell me on what basis, Hale. Procedure 4.2 says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. I'm writing down that you're refusing to change it.
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.
Fine. Then I'll take your refusal upstairs, and I'll want it in an email tonight. Unless you have something with a date on it, Hale, that's the end of this.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.
"The answer is no." I'm writing that down, word for word, and it goes to the principal with the fact that Owen was never heard. Do you have one document, Hale, or is that all of it?
